newsitem.title: FINLAND: Pohjola says Suomi approves Salama sale.
newsitem.headline: Pohjola says Suomi approves Salama sale.

text.p: Finnish insurer Vakuutusosakeyhtio Pohjola said on Tuesday that mutual life assurance firm Suomi's representatives assembly had approved the sale of Suomi's Salama unit to Pohjola.
"The proposal was approved with the votes 45 to 24," Pohjola CEO Iiro Viinanen told a news conference.
Approval by the representatives assembly followed Suomi's supervisory board's backing last week of the restructuring plan initiated by Pohjola in January.

Suomi's supervisory board decided on April 29 that Suomi would sell its 92 percent stake in Salama to Pohjola for 537.3 million markka, and that it would give up underwriting new business against compensation of 54 million markka.
The purchase of Salama is part of a wider restructuring plan which will eventually lead to a takeover of Suomi.

Non-life insurer Pohjola has said it wants to ride a boom in life-insurance but has not been able to do so since it is associated through cross-ownerships with life-insurer Suomi, which it says does not have enough solvency capital to fund strong growth.
On the other hand, Pohjola's non-life operation has surplus solvency capital, some of which it wants to transfer to its new life unit.
At end-1996, its 6.43 billion markka total solvency capital was 2.5 times liabilities.
